info.description:
One deployable, fourteen modules (ADR-003). Conventions that hold everywhere:

- **`entrance_id` is the only tenant key** (ADR-005). Every resource resolves to exactly one entrance; nothing is addressable across entrances.
- **Every write carries `Idempotency-Key`** (PM-SYS-014). A queued offline action replays without duplicating.
- **Money is integer minor units in EUR** (PM-FEE-016). No floats anywhere.
- **A refusal names the rule that refused** — `rule_id` in the problem body, so a client can explain the law rather than say "invalid".
- **A statutory precondition cannot be skipped** (PM-SYS-006); 409 is the refusal, and the only alternative is a recorded, audited deviation.
- **Statutory documents are Bulgarian** (PM-SYS-003) whatever the Accept-Language.

amount_minor.description: integer minor units — never a float (PM-FEE-016, ADR-006)

IdealParts.description: exact decimal percentage, four places per docs/RULES.md §4

Problem.description: RFC 9457. A refusal names the rule that refused.

rule_id.description: the rule that refused, when a rule refused

status.description: PROVISIONAL until the absentee window closes (PM-VOTE-013)

bill_comparison.description: their figures against ours, per unit — Gate 1, on every import

IntakeField.description: a domain field a fee sheet can carry — the target of any column mapping (ADR-012), fixed by our rules (PM-BOOK-002, PM-ORG-002), never by one spreadsheet

csv.description: the sheet — only its header row is read, to propose a mapping

MappingProposal.description: a proposed column → field mapping for one sheet, plus what could not be placed (ADR-012): a human confirms or corrects it and returns it on the dry-run/commit. Nothing is dropped silently, and a required field no column carries is named so the import cannot proceed

mapping.description: source column, as written → domain field

unmapped_columns.description: columns the profiler could not place — surfaced for a human, never dropped

missing_required.description: required fields no column carries — mapped by hand before the import proceeds
